methods.label: Interpret the zero discriminant
methods.explanation:
The discriminant \(\Delta\) is the quantity under the square root in the quadratic formula. When \(\Delta=0\), the \(+\sqrt\Delta\) and \(-\sqrt\Delta\) terms are both zero, so the two roots coincide.

Here the quadratic coefficient is \(1\), the linear coefficient is \(2\sqrt3\), and the given discriminant is zero. Therefore
\[
x=\frac{-2\sqrt3\pm\sqrt0}{2}=-\sqrt3.
\]
Both roots are the same real number, so they are real and equal, choice A.
